rubric.none: specs are updated alongside code; spot checks find no divergence.
rubric.low: minor gaps; specs trail code slightly but remain a reliable guide.
rubric.moderate: specs noticeably lag; parts of codebase are no longer described.
rubric.high: specs are stale or abandoned while code moves on.

ratings.rationale: The specs tree contains only the OpenClaw and ACE MCP slices and was last touched 155 commits before the pin. The intervening history includes a PydanticAI migration, restored and expanded CLI/integrations, provenance models, and runtime/sub-agent work with no corresponding specs entries.

OpenSpec is active and was updated two commits before the pin. The only later changes are narrowly scoped test de-flaking fixes, so spot checks show no product behavior moving beyond the current specs.

The superpowers specs stopped changing 335 commits before the pin. Subsequent code adds advertising projects, narration, screenplay-source workflows, and MiniMax and Kling providers, while the pinned spec filenames contain none of those major capabilities.

Only two April feature designs are present, while 108 later commits add image quality control, per-page templates, provider overrides, batch import behavior, and substantial desktop packaging/export behavior. Large areas of the newer product are not represented by the specs.

After the latest feature spec, the pinned branch adds documentation and capability-audit material only; the comparison shows no code files changing. With code stationary and the documentation becoming more detailed, spot checks found no divergence.

This repository has an extensive active OpenSpec corpus, and the pin itself updates OpenSpec while converging Kimi session identity and UI workflows. Matching Kimi, Kanban, and session change/spec areas are present at the exact pin.

The Scout designs remain recognizable and the later Scout changes are small sender and migration corrections. Twenty-one post-spec commits also contain unrelated security, deployment, and worker fixes, creating minor undocumented gaps without invalidating the feature specs.

The two OTA designs are older than 30 mostly release, build, and corrective commits. Those changes introduce small mobile and desktop behavior gaps, but there is no broad post-spec architecture replacement and the OTA material remains usable.

The large Kiro corpus is recent, but 79 subsequent commits implement audit-log index management and fuzzy username suggestions without matching feature specs in the pinned spec tree. Existing specs are substantial, yet the active branch has noticeable undescribed product work.

The specification and plan collection is broad, and the pin itself updates it while adding an explicit CI and pre-push drift gate for Debian QML dependencies. There are no later commits to create divergence.

OpenSpec was last changed roughly six months and 309 commits before the pin. The code subsequently gained a new alignment service, audio-only UI, search/replace, logging, native-service refactors, and a v3 documentation structure, none represented in the small pinned OpenSpec set.

Only ten commits follow the latest superpowers update, mostly targeted refactors and fixes in areas already covered by recent Logitech and input plans. A haptic debug control and receiver handoff create minor gaps, while architecture documentation is also refreshed.

The extensive OpenSpec corpus was current until four commits before the pin. ZCode, CodeArts Agent, Qwen command-format, and skills.sh publication then changed code and documentation without corresponding pinned OpenSpec changes, a small but concrete lag.

All fourteen use cases were updated together before the pin. The ten later commits are grammar, dependency, workflow, and requirements-document updates rather than application behavior, so no use-case/code divergence was found.

The three current feature designs were updated three days before the pin. The sole later commit is a narrow wildcard-window bug fix in tmux code and does not contradict the status, cache, or enriched-session-name specs.

A Soniox design and same-day follow-up plan cover the principal new provider work. Nine later commits refine validation, setup links, branding, and detected-language display, leaving slight implementation detail lag but not making the design unreliable.

The three steering documents have not changed for more than a year, while the later history migrates Bedrock models and changes hosted item-image deployment and server configuration. The small codebase limits the scope, but portions of its current runtime and deployment are no longer captured by steering.

The documentation is broad and was updated eight commits before the pin. Later core work is one dynamic-parallel tracing fix, while the large file delta is dominated by BMAD assets and new examples; those additions create minor coverage gaps without displacing the documented framework capabilities.

The specs are recent and still cover most major product slices, but twelve later commits add an end-to-end stale-knowledge-graph warning and broaden Rust ignore behavior without a corresponding stale-graph design. That is a noticeable new behavior area beyond the pinned specs.

The planning system is extensive and the exact pin updates it alongside durable inbound receive attempts and cancellation behavior. Current implementation plans for that state machine and receive-attempt slice are present at the pin, with no later code to diverge.

The repository has recent cloud-simulation and wkbench designs, plans, and runbooks. Twenty-seven subsequent commits harden queues, budgets, evidence, readiness, and warmup behavior within those described systems, producing detailed lag but no major undescribed subsystem.

The large superpowers corpus was updated one day before the pin. Only a Justfile fix and a GLX-pbuffer implementation revert follow it; the revert can leave a small mismatch with recent rendering plans, but the rest of the specifications remain current.
